newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House passes resolution urging Mobutu to quit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House passes resolution urging Mobutu to quit.

text.p: The U.S. House of Representatives unanimously passed a resolution on Thursday urging a peaceful end to Zaire's civil war and calling for the resignation of President Mobutu Sese Seko.

"Today the U.S. House of Representatives goes on record saying formally that Mobutu must go. He must go now. He has no role to play in Zaire," said Representative Ed Royce, chairman of the International Relations Subcommittee on Africa.

Royce, a California Republican, said the resolution was directed against Mobutu, but it also called on the Clinton administration to support democratic, multiparty elections in the war-torn African nation.
Zaire's warring sides met in South Africa last week and said they agreed on the need for a ceasefire and democratic elections. There is no sign of a quick resumption of talks.
The United States last week signalled that Mobutu should step down, effectively ending a decades-old alliance with the African strongman.
Royce said the central African nation was vital to stability in the region. "And if Zaire falls into chaos, it could lead to a massive humanitarian crisis," he said.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns on Monday told reporters Washington was urging the rebels led by Laurent Kabila and Mobutu's government to resume negotiations in South Africa.
